research_context.used: Tikaradze Theorem1 is comparison context for actual invariant orders; it is not used to infer division-ring quotient rigidity.
General Weyl index symmetry is context only. The finite-quotient left/right equality is proved directly here using Artin bounds and valuation-branch residue independence.

coverage_boundary: Exact discriminants and squarefreeness, retained classical cubic chart, first-order rational Weyl and finite-group action identities, a cyclic Galois residue control, a pole-bearing valuation-moving involution, branch selectors, averaged residues and finite subgroup normalizers. Universal branch approximation, residue Galois descent, characteristic-zero kernel rigidity, Artin dimension bounds, generic/completed index accounting, centralizer and automorphism rigidity, all-degree Long exclusion, stabilization and rational source/target transport use written proofs. The controls do not prove group or operator exhaustion. The conclusion excludes direct finite fixed-division-ring models; a larger Galois closure with an intermediate subgroup-fixed source, different nonsymmetric embeddings, and general higher-rank matrix actions remain open. No actual Long carrier is built.
